title: PlainID Enterprise Policies
subtitle: WHO/WHAT/WHEN, structured Rego, PDP APIs
content:
🧭 WHO / WHAT / WHEN (Wizard, Verified)

PlainID's Policy Wizard structures every policy as: WHO (dynamic groups get access), WHAT (asset types + action-ruleset combinations), WHEN (conditions). Access type is Allow or Restrict; dynamic authorization and SaaS management are separate policy uses. A policy without WHAT is invalid — WHO alone grants nothing.

PlainID structured Rego: dynamic_group + ruleset + condition 
# Last verified: 2026-09 vs PlainID structured-Rego docs
# WHO: Gold + Standard external customers
dynamic_group(identity) if {
  identity.template == "User"
  identity["User_Type"] == "External"
  identity["Membership_Type"] == "Gold"
}

# WHAT: own accounts (View) + own cards (Manage, View)
ruleset(asset, identity, requestParams, action) if {
  asset.template == "Bank Accounts"
  asset["account_owner"] == identity["Userid_identity"]
  action.id in ["View"]
}

# WHEN: step-up MFA condition
condition_request(requestParams, identity) if {
  requestParams["Auth_Method"] == "MFA"
}
# Last verified: 2026-09 vs PlainID structured-Rego docs # WHO: Gold + Standard external customers dynamic_group(identity) if { identity.template == "User" identity["User_Type"] == "External" identity["Membership_Type"] == "Gold" } # WHAT: own accounts (View) + own cards (Manage, View) ruleset(asset, identity, requestParams, action) if { asset.template == "Bank Accounts" asset["account_owner"] == identity["Userid_identity"] action.id in ["View"] } # WHEN: step-up MFA condition condition_request(requestParams, identity) if { requestParams["Auth_Method"] == "MFA" }

📨 PDP APIs: Permit-Deny and Resolution

  • Permit/Deny (incl. V5 API-access endpoint): the original REST call (headers, URI path array, body) is forwarded; API matchers/mappers extract AssetID + request attributes; identity mappers parse the JWT. Returns permit/deny + optional deny reasons and asset attributes. (Per PlainID V5 API-access docs — confirm path/payload against your tenant version.)
  • Policy Resolution: answers what filters for this user? for SQL/search/big-data enforcement done by another system — returns allowed attribute-filters, not just booleans.
  • Multi-identity evaluation (Scope-gated): up to three identities from different templates (human + agent + app) evaluated with AND semantics — but only when Use Multiple Identities Combination is enabled on the Scope (disabled by default). More than three identities = request error. In default single-identity mode, other templates' rules are ignored — an agent riding along unevaluated is an over-grant, not defense in depth.
APIAnswersStaleness / failure mode
Permit/Deny (+V5)May they do this?Real-time per call; PDP-down must fail closed (deny + alert)
Policy ResolutionWhat filters for them?Filters computed at call time; re-resolve on policy/attribute change, never cache across revocations
User Access TokenSession credentialNOT real-time; large asset sets hit memory/perf limits — revalidate for high-risk actions
Unavailable identity sourceLimited responseMissing attributes resolve against what IS available — treat limited responses as deny-by-default unless explicitly risk-accepted

🔍 Critical Review Notes

  • Allow vs Restrict (documented, no Cedar analogy): Allow grants when all aspects match; Restrict denies when its settings are met. A standalone Restrict denies matching requests — audit every Scope's Allow+Restrict interaction explicitly, and test Restrict-only scopes rather than assuming a counterpart.
  • Native policies (Snowflake/Databricks): PlainID can push vendor-native masking/RLS — same tags/table/column mapping discipline as Immuta; review generated native code like any migration artifact.
  • AI Policy Builder: natural-language authoring generates the same model — but generated policies get the same tests and reviews as hand-written ones. Convenience is not verification.

🔒 Lock-in / Bill / Exit (Read Before You Commit)

  • Lock-in (documented): Scopes, entityTypeIds, asset templates, and wizard-authored policies live in the PlainID control plane; enforcement couples to PDP tenancy/region. Rego-export exists for structured policies, but wizard-only artifacts do not round-trip as code.
  • Bill (estimate — confirm current pricing): per-decision PDP volume plus caching strategy; PDP-per-tool-call agent patterns (Lesson 22) multiply call counts — budget latency AND invoice together, with fail-closed availability design.
  • Exit (documented pattern): exported structured Rego + attribute feeds port to embedded OPA/Cedar with a rewrite of matchers/mappers; SaaS-native policies rewrite to vendor RLS/masking. Keep identity-attribute pipelines vendor-neutral from day one.
🎮 Try it in the Policy Lab → Step the Sara support-analyst request through WHO → WHAT → WHEN. Use the controls under the canvas to switch scenarios and watch the verdict change.

questions.question: A PlainID policy names a dynamic group but no asset type. What happens?

options.text: Invalid — WHO without WHAT grants nothing
It grants everything to the group

questions.explanation: Docs-verified validity rule: a policy must include at least one of Identity / Agent / Control-or-Guardrail AND at least one WHAT (asset, tool, or action). WHO alone grants nothing.

questions.question: In the structured-Rego sample, what does condition_request(Auth_Method == MFA) enforce?

options.text: WHEN: the policy grants only under step-up MFA context
It grants MFA devices admin rights

questions.explanation: Conditions are the WHEN gate: same WHO+WHAT, different context → different verdict. Context-aware authZ without code changes.

questions.question: Your enforcement point is a search engine needing per-user result filters. Which PDP API?

options.text: Policy Resolution — returns allowed attribute-filters for external enforcement
A cached permit/deny boolean per user (stale the moment attributes change)

questions.explanation: Resolution answers 'what may they see?' (filters) vs permit-deny's 'may they do this?' (boolean). Bulk-data systems need the former.

questions.question: A Scope has Use Multiple Identities Combination enabled. A request carries human Sara + agent support-bot + app helpdesk. How are they evaluated?

options.text: Together with AND semantics — each must satisfy its template's rules (max 3 templates)
OR semantics — any one passing allows
Identities are concatenated into one string

questions.explanation: With the Scope flag ON: unified decision, strict AND across templates (disabled by default — in single-identity mode the extra identities are ignored, an over-grant). Max 3 templates; more is a request error.

questions.question: The AI assistant drafts a policy from a natural-language prompt. What is required before deploy?

options.text: Same tests, review, and schema checks as hand-written policy
Nothing — AI output is always correct

questions.explanation: Authoring convenience changes who writes, not what ships. Generated policy is untrusted input until verified (Lesson 20).

questions.question: A policy allows all engineers on all repos with no conditions. What's missing for least privilege?

options.text: Scoped WHAT (which repos and actions) plus WHEN (conditions) — broad/broad/none is a smell

questions.explanation: WHO/WHAT/WHEN is a completeness check. A policy with no WHAT scope and no WHEN is a grant waiting for an incident.

questions.question: Resolution returns filters your search engine cannot express (regex on analyzed text). Options?

options.text: Pre-filter where expressible, post-filter the remainder, and document the gap

questions.explanation: External enforcement is only as strong as the engine's filter language. Gaps get compensating post-filters, explicitly.

questions.question: An MFA condition reads requestParams Auth_Method. Where must that value come from?

options.text: A trusted mapper (IdP or session) — never client-asserted input
The user typing it into a form

questions.explanation: Conditions are only as trustworthy as their attributes. Client-asserted MFA is theater with extra steps.
